title: Chaupai at nightfall
hookLine: the Benti Chaupai, now prayed as darkness comes
last: WHY WORRY — EVEN THE ROCK-CREATURES EAT.

lines: LAST THING AT NIGHT: THE ROUNDS.
THE NIGHT STILL FINDS WAYS IN.
cards: Last thing at night, in a lot of houses, someone does the rounds. Back door locked. Stove knob checked, twice.
A glance through the curtain at the street. A child's door pushed open an inch, just to hear the breathing. Nobody calls it a prayer.
But it's one of the oldest things a household does: before the dark, make sure everyone is inside and kept. And the night still finds other ways in: a hospital ward, an empty flat, a long drive home.

teach.h: FROM THE NINE SHABADS TO THE TENTH GURU.
teach.b: After the nine shabads, Rehras moves from the Guru Granth Sahib to the Tenth Guru's words: the Benti Chaupai of Guru Gobind Singh, the same prayer many Sikhs said this morning.
You spent ten days with it earlier on this path.

teach.h: GIVE ME YOUR HAND AND KEEP ME.
teach.b: In paraphrase: protect me, giving me your hand. May the wish of my heart be fulfilled. May my mind stay at your feet.
Take me as your own, and look after me. In the morning, those words go out with you into the day. In Rehras, they're said as the light is going, and they land differently.

teach.h: AT DUSK, WHAT YOU ASK FOR IS SHELTER.
teach.b: Shelter is what you ask for at dusk. Whoever does the rounds at night isn't looking for adventure. They want the door shut, a lamp on, someone keeping watch.
That's the posture of the Chaupai in Rehras. And it isn't a frightened prayer. It was written by a Guru who faced real armies and real nights, and it never pretends danger isn't there.
It simply asks, in the middle of it, to be kept.

teach.h: EVERY OTHER DOOR LEFT; YOURS AT NIGHT.
teach.b: Right after it, Rehras carries the short savaiya and dohra you met at the close of that block: since I took hold of your feet, I look to no one else; leaving every other door, I've come to yours. So the order is a shape.
Shelter me with your hand. I've stopped knocking on other doors. Yours is the one I'm at as night comes.

how: In Rehras Sahib, after the nine shabads, Sikhs recite Guru Gobind Singh's Benti Chaupai, followed by a savaiya and a dohra; it is also one of the morning banis, and many Sikhs say it before a journey or at night.

o: a short hymn sung only at Sikh weddings
a four-sided seat for the Guru Granth Sahib
four-part verse: the Tenth Guru's plea for shelter

games.q: the Chaupai at dusk — tap the pairs.
p: Guru Gobind Singh's prayer for protection
protect me, giving me your hand
every other door left, yours reached

s: the Chaupai is said only in the evening
it's one of the morning banis too, and returns inside Rehras at dusk.
in Rehras the Chaupai follows the nine shabads
after So Dar and So Purakh, the Tenth Guru's prayer.
the Chaupai pretends danger isn't real
it was written by a Guru who faced real armies; it asks to be kept in the middle of danger.

games.q: the light is going and you're far from home. what does the Chaupai ask for?
o: to be fearless and need no one.
a hand to protect you, and to be taken as His own.
for the night to be cut short.
games.why: protect me, giving me your hand; take me as your own and look after me: shelter, not bravado.

practice: If you have the Chaupai on your phone or in a gutka, read its first two lines slowly: hamree karo haath dai rachhaa, pooran hoe chit kee ichhaa; if not, hold their meaning, protect me, giving me your hand, may the wish of my heart be fulfilled.
Then picture the coming night, where you'll sleep, who's near, what you're carrying into it, and let the lines rest over it like a roof.

wordCard.voice: Chaupai, Guru Gobind Singh's Benti Chaupai, said in the morning and again inside Rehras as darkness comes: protect me, giving me your hand.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: rachhaa, protection; hamree karo haath dai rachhaa, protect me, giving me your hand.

carryVoice: Your line: shelter for the night. Not a frightened prayer; a kept one. Day four hundred fifteen.

sources.ref: Sikh Rehat Maryada, on the contents of Rehras
